newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares slide to 1300pts as volume drops.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares slide to 1300pts as volume drops.

text.p: Greek equities retreated 1.33 percent on Tuesday, pulled back by a weak construction sector and softer bank and industrial shares as trading volume dropped to 10.5 billion drachmas. Monday was a market holiday.

Back from a long holiday weekend, the market started firmer in early trade but the general share index started heading south in mid-session and gave up 17.6 points with market watchers expecting stocks to consolidate this week.

"Some were expecting a rally in the construction sector after Athens made it to the shortlist of five candidate cities to host the 2004 Olympics. But the market didn't give this opportunity," said Nick Verras, director of private banking at Interbank.
"I see the market consolidating in the short term, trading plus or minus 50 points from where it is now. Overall, the fundamentals point to the upside," he said.

Greece's CPI-based inflation fell to 6.6 percent year-on-year in February from 6.8 percent in January. And January wholesale price inflation eased to 3.1 percent year-on-year from 3.9 percent in December 1996, the National Statistics Service (NSS) said.
On Friday, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) picked Athens to the shortlist of five candidate cities to host the Olympics 2004 Games along with Buenos Aires, Rome, Stockholm and Cape Town.
The Athens general share index was closed 1.33 percent or 17.60 points lower at 1301.59 points from Friday's 1319.19 after opening at 1323.61. The session's low was at 1297.71.
Turnover dropped to 10.51 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares. Decliners led advancers 180 to 41 with 20 issues unchanged on 241 traded.
Construction fell 5.35 percent, banks slipped 1.48 percent with industrials settling 1.47 percent lower. Small caps lost 3.01 percent.
Rebels in Albania dismissed President Sali Berisha's political deal to end the conflict insisting they would not down any arms unless he resigned.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 974.00-1012.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, gained 50 drachmas to close at 5,770.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $38.22-$39.92. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 1,406-1,582 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 10,756-11,322 drachmas. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
